The metacognitive accuracy task was programmed in MATLAB (MathWorks) using Psychtoolbox
Two circles (diameter 5.1 degrees) with small crosshairs in their centers appeared at eccentricities of ±8.9° for 1 s.
Participants sat in front of a computer screen at a comfortable viewing distance and completed a perception task.
If the left circle contained more dots, the participant pressed the ‘left arrow’ key; if the right circle contained more dots, the participant pressed the ‘right arrow’ key.
Participants made a two-choice discrimination judgment about what they had perceived, followed by a confidence rating in their decision.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to guess which circle, left or right, contained more dots by pressing the corresponding left- or right-arrow key, followed by a confidence rating in their decision.

source_definition.value: Metacognitive accuracy was defined as log(meta-d′/d′), where meta-d′ is type 2 sensitivity to discriminate one's own correct from incorrect judgments and d′ is type 1 sensitivity to distinguish stimulus alternatives.

spans.text: meta- d’ is a measure of type 2 sensitivity (i.e., the degree to which participants can discriminate their own correct from incorrect judgments) that is expressed in the same units as type 1 sensitivity ( d’ ) (i.e., the degree to which participants can distinguish stimulus alternatives).

model_settings.value: Whole-brain multiple regression analysis in SPM8; age, depression, and cigarette smoking history were entered as covariates of no interest. Significance was set at p < 0.05, family-wise-error corrected at the voxel level, with an additional p < 0.001 uncorrected threshold and a 25-voxel minimum.
